name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,568

clue.text: Dismiss sandwich possibly with no end of chicken

indicators.note: 'with no' says the snack goes without something, so a letter is taken out of it
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter of the bird is the one removed

blocks.note: a sandwich is one example of a snack
the final letter of chicken

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a sandwich because the chicken filling has been skimped on at one end.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the last letter of chicken out of SNACK to leave SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the sack is to fire them from a job, so the verb sack means discharge an employee.

clue.text: One's forte is to be powerful executive?

blocks.note: strong means powerful
suit is slang for a business executive in a suit

explanation.surface: Someone's talent, it seems, is being a mighty businessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong suit is the thing a person does best, from the card game term, matching forte as a noun.

clue.text: Coarseness in heartless song when following college rugby

indicators.note: heartless means without a heart, so the middle letter of the song goes

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for college
RU stands for Rugby Union
a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A rugby team's vulgar song is sung after a college match.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartless removes only the single middle letter of an odd-length word; in the surface it seems to describe the song's tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudity is the quality of being crude, vulgar or unrefined, a noun just like coarseness.

clue.text: Conference is not durable after disruption

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown out of its usual order, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A meeting turns out to be a flimsy affair once it has been interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A round table is a meeting or discussion where participants meet as equals, a type of conference.

clue.text: Individual defends James, maybe, describing a legitimate goal?

indicators.note: a defender stands around what they protect, so the individual surrounds the other name

blocks.note: the start of one, an individual
Sid James was a British comic actor famous from the Carry On films
the end of one

explanation.surface: A lone defender's play suggests the goal James scored should stand.
explanation.walkthrough: SID goes inside ONE. James looks like a footballer's surname; it is the surname behind a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a goal scored onside is allowed, so onside is the adjective for a valid, legitimate goal.

clue.text: Brass left by expert in jewellery

definitions.note: the answer is one item of jewellery

blocks.note: brass and neck both mean cheek or nerve
L is the abbreviation for left
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Some brass has been left with a skilled jeweller.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass here is British slang for impudence, as is neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is a chain or string of beads worn around the throat, a common piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Bullish sign (not half) in Greek character

indicators.note: not half means without half of it, so the second half of the sign is removed

blocks.note: Taurus, the Bull, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A sign of a rising stock market appears in Greek letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Bullish suggests the stock market but refers to the Bull of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the equivalent of the English T.

clue.text: Someone of less than stellar status, a continuing irritation?

definitions.text: Someone of less than stellar status

blocks.clueFragment: Someone of less than stellar status
blocks.note: first meaning: a celebrity in the second tier, below the A-list stars
second meaning: a sore bubble on the skin that keeps rubbing

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity who is a constant nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as B-LISTER for the first meaning; the question mark flags the loose second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-rank celebrity is a B-lister, and a blister is a sore bump on skin that keeps irritating.

clue.text: Leaders in exchange undercut rates over newish currency

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so the first letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Cheap exchange rates undermine a young currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro was launched in 1999, relatively recent among currencies, so it is a fairly new form of money.

clue.text: Brand, say, having revised income need

indicators.note: something revised has been altered, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A product brand has had its revenue requirement adjusted.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand is not a product name but Jo Brand, the British stand-up comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Jo Brand is a well-known female stand-up comic, so she is an example of a woman comedian.

clue.text: Harsh Republican, American, acquiring a posh firm

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the American abbreviation holds the following letters inside it

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
US is short for American, as in the United States
taken as written
U means upper-class, the crossword shorthand for posh
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A grating Republican politician from America buys into an upmarket business.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas hide that Republican and American join up to swallow the rest. U for upper-class (posh) dates from the 1950s U and non-U debate about British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous describes a loud, rough, grating noise, so it matches harsh as an adjective for sounds.

clue.text: Dressmaker drops half of tutu, one accompanying package?

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so the dressmaker loses some letters

blocks.note: a couturier designs and makes fashionable clothes
tutu is two identical halves, each of two letters

explanation.surface: A dressmaker cuts down a ballet skirt, then sends it off in a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TU from the middle of COUTURIER. 'Package' is a package holiday, not a parcel, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is a travel guide employed to look after tourists on a package holiday, accompanying the group throughout.

clue.text: Green local removing latest sign of pollutant

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so a letter is dropped from the word for local
the latest sign is the last one to appear, so only the final letter is wanted

blocks.note: a local is a native of a place
the final letter of pollutant

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded resident cleans up the last traces of contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks environmental beside pollutant; here it means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of inexperienced and easily fooled is a synonym of naive, unworldly or innocent.

clue.text: Gentle priest backed by chapter in appointed time

indicators.note: in places the priest and chapter inside the appointed time

blocks.note: the opening of a date, an appointed time
Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel
C is the abbreviation for chapter
the rest of the date surrounding the inserted letters

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered cleric is supported by his chapter at the scheduled service.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI followed by C goes inside DATE, the appointed time.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate means soft, light or tender in touch, so it can replace gentle as an adjective.

clue.text: Scam for now unregulated? It's a potentially difficult situation

indicators.note: unregulated means without controls, so the letters run free into a new order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A fraud nobody controls at present is bound to cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a can of worms is an idiom for starting a complicated problem that is hard to contain.

clue.text: Top wine pro arranged programme for presentation

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A leading sommelier has set up a tasting schedule to present.
explanation.walkthrough: Programme here means a computer program, the British spelling covering both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: PowerPoint is Microsoft software for building slide shows, a computer application for giving talks.

clue.text: Block presenting problem for observers circling road

indicators.note: circling means going around something, so the road sits inside the first word

blocks.note: the start of a stye, an eye infection, a problem for those who observe with eyes
the M1, written MI, is Britain's first motorway
the end of the stye

explanation.surface: A roadblock causes trouble for people watching traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: MI goes inside STYE. Observers here means eyes, the things that observe.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie someone is to obstruct or thwart their plans, so it is a verb meaning hinder or prevent.

clue.text: Outline for development namely shown by woman on carnival site

blocks.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
Ena is a woman's name
Rio de Janeiro hosts a famous annual carnival

explanation.surface: A woman sketches out a plan for the area where the carnival is held.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a written sketch of a plot or a projected sequence of events, a plan for how things may unfold.

clue.text: Wine and Indian food put in temporary facilities?

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
aloo is potato in Indian cooking

explanation.surface: Drinks and curry are laid on in a makeshift venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Facilities is a euphemism for toilets, and Portaloo is a British brand of portable toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portaloo is a portable lavatory put up at outdoor events, a short-term toilet.

clue.text: Bell, perhaps, in IOW place emitting second note

indicators.note: emitting means sending out, so a letter leaves the Isle of Wight town's name

blocks.note: taken as written
Ventnor is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast
the second N in the town's name, N standing for note

explanation.surface: Something rings out at a place on the Isle of Wight, sounding a second note.
explanation.walkthrough: IN then VENTNOR without its second N. Bell is Alexander Graham Bell, not a ringing bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with the telephone, making him an example of someone who devises new machines.

clue.text: Eastern European revolutionary goes round with destructive types

indicators.note: a revolution turns something over, so the European is read from end to start
going round something encloses it, so the reversed word holds the word for with

blocks.note: a Slav is a member of a people of Eastern Europe
and means together with

explanation.surface: An Eastern European rebel hangs around with wreckers.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary looks like a noun describing a rebel, but it only signals turning the European round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandals deliberately damage property, so they are people given to wanton destruction.

clue.text: Old lot touring Luxembourg recently

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the word for lot goes round the country's letter

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the start of fate, one's lot in life
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
the rest of fate

explanation.surface: A group of elderly people have been on a trip around Luxembourg lately.
explanation.walkthrough: O, then FATE wrapped around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late is an idiom meaning lately or in the recent past, an adverbial phrase like recently.

clue.text: Mean TV detective found in decline?

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the detective sits within the word for decline

blocks.note: the start of age, to decline with the years
Vera Stanhope is the detective in the British TV drama Vera
the rest of age

explanation.surface: A nasty television sleuth is shown to be past it.
explanation.walkthrough: Decline here means grow old, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean as a noun is the arithmetic average, the sum of values divided by their count.

clue.text: Cathedral authority taking care of priest's assistant

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the cathedral figure holds the abbreviation inside

blocks.note: the start of dean, the head of a cathedral chapter
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
the end of dean

explanation.surface: A senior cleric looks after the priest's helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest who helps with services and parish duties.

clue.text: Loosen a French item of furniture

blocks.note: un is the French for a
a settle is a wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: Someone is told to slacken a piece of French furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to disturb or dislodge something fixed, making it less firm, which is a looser sense of loosen.

clue.text: Not tense, become healthier showing advantage?

indicators.note: not tells you to go without the following abbreviation, so it is struck out

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
to tone up is to get fitter

explanation.surface: Advice to relax and get fit, which will give you an edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T from TONE UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one up means being a step ahead of a rival, holding the upper hand in a contest.

clue.text: Precious stone placed in top altar

indicators.note: placed in means sitting inside, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the end of top and the start of altar

explanation.surface: A gem has been set on the high altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone known for its shifting rainbow colours, a classic semi-precious stone.

clue.text: High-spirited pal fully tipsy after draining single litre

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order
draining empties something out, so the litre is removed from the letters

blocks.note: the anagram fodder before the litre goes
L is the abbreviation for litre; just one of the two Ls goes

explanation.surface: A cheerful friend is thoroughly drunk after downing a litre in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful means full of fun and good humour, describing someone frisky or lively, like high-spirited.

clue.text: Fellow has lapse on field in bewilderment

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
OG is an own goal, a footballer's lapse that scores for the other side

explanation.surface: A player is baffled after making a mistake on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fog means being confused and unable to think clearly, so fog stands for mental confusion.

clue.text: Place for military restricted dry aperitif

indicators.note: restricted means cut short, so the word for dry loses its final letter

blocks.note: a camp is where soldiers are based
arid means dry

explanation.surface: An army base has a limited supply of dry pre-dinner drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is a bitter red Italian liqueur, typically drunk before a meal as an appetiser drink.

clue.text: Fall back with louder song being played

indicators.note: playing with something reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An audience retreats as a noisier tune strikes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose ground is an idiom meaning to retreat or lose an advantage, as an army falling back does.

clue.text: Some love starry waistcoat found on Broadway?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the letters sit within them

blocks.note: the end of love and the start of starry

explanation.surface: A sparkly waistcoat worn on stage in a New York show.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadway stands for America, where vest is the word for what Britons call a waistcoat; in Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a vest is the sleeveless garment worn under a jacket, the British waistcoat.
